summary: Timezone offset during scheduled multi-region batch embeddings caused mid-cycle credit loss and invoice variance
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightPath Analytics reported an unexpected mid-cycle consumption of reserved credits after a scheduled multi-region batch embedding job. They observed a ~12% deduction from their reserved hourly credits window leading to a negative provisional balance and a flagged invoice variance.

Impact:
- Immediate: Customer's monthly provisional invoice shows a -$1,820 line attributed to 'usage adjustment' for the batch run on 2026-03-11 23:00 UTC. Customer reports they had sufficient reserved credits.
- Business: Customer is on a dedicated reserved plan; unexpected reserve consumption erodes trust and could trigger billing disputes.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: rh-dedicated-prod-1 (us-east)
- Batch job: nightly multi-region embed job (cron: 0 23 * * * in local time for customer)
- Model: openembed-v2-512 (quantized)
- Metering pipeline: batch-worker -> postback-service -> hourly-accumulator -> billing-reconciler

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Customer schedules a nightly batch of 1.2M texts at 2026-03-11 19:00 EST which corresponds to 2026-03-11 23:00 UTC.
2) Job completes and posts postbacks to our meter endpoint.
3) Next hourly reconciliation run attributes ~12% of the job to the previous hourly window due to a timestamp offset.
4) Customer sees reserve credits consumed mid-window and receives provisional negative balance notice.

Observed behavior:
- Postbacks from the batch worker contain X-Client-Timezone: "America/New_York" but timestamps are sent as local epoch_millis instead of normalized UTC. The postback service accepted the payload and used the received epoch to bucket into hourly-accumulator without normalization.

Expected behavior:
- All postbacks should be normalized to UTC in postback-service before hourly bucketing; reserved credits should be consumed only within the correct hourly window.

Relevant IDs / Logs:
- Customer job id: BP-embed-run-20260311-23
- Metering request examples (redacted): request_ids: [mtr-15f7, mtr-15f8, mtr-16a2]
- Billing line id: INV-PROV-20260311-1820

Customer note:
"We scheduled the job for 7PM EST; our billing team expected consumption in the 23:00 UTC window. The provisional invoice indicates part of the job consumed into the 22:00 window, which drained reserved credits and triggered an autopay hold. We need credits reapplied and guidance to prevent recurrence."
comments: 2026-03-12 08:12 - Sofia Martinez (Support): Initial triage and acknowledgement sent to customer. Requested full job logs and sample postback payloads. Provided temporary escalation to Billing SLA. (sla_due: 2026-03-14).

2026-03-12 09:05 - Customer (BrightPath Analytics - billing@brightpath.com): Provided gzipped postback archive and their local scheduler cron. Noted that their batch library emits timestamps in milliseconds without timezone suffix.

2026-03-12 11:40 - Priya Shah (SRE): Ingested sample postbacks into dev metering pipeline. Observed epoch_ms values that, when interpreted as local epoch, shift events by -3600 or +3600 depending on DST. Created a repro harness. Linking logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/sup/SUP-314159/trace

2026-03-13 13:22 - Kenji Tanaka (Billing Eng): Found hourly-accumulator applies 'window_key = floor(epoch_ms / 3600000)' without verifying timezone normalization. Hourly recon task trusts postback-provided epoch. Opened PR to normalize at postback-service. Reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/412

2026-03-13 16:10 - Support (Sofia): Notified customer that engineering identified root cause (postback timestamp normalization bug) and that we will provisionally re-apply reserved credits for the affected window while a permanent fix is rolled out. Asked customer to confirm if they want immediate manual credit reallocation.
2026-03-14 09:30 - BrightPath (Billing contact): Confirmed they want immediate credit reallocation and asked for ETA on fix.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Batch clients emitting local epoch_ms got interpreted as UTC, causing events to be bucketed into adjacent hourly windows during DST transitions.

Steps performed:
- Replayed sample postbacks to dev accumulator and reproduced mis-bucketing.
- Queried hourly_aggregate table: SELECT sum(tokens) FROM hourly_aggregate WHERE window_start BETWEEN '2026-03-11 22:00:00' AND '2026-03-11 23:00:00' AND org_id = 'org-brightpath'; observed +12% spike.
- Checked postback-service code path: no timezone header parsing; it trusts numeric epoch_ms and casts to UTC without client hinting.
- Confirmed dedicated cluster ingested messages unaltered (no proxy rewrite).

Temporary mitigation options considered:
1) Recompute hourly aggregates by re-normalizing postbacks to UTC and reapply credits (safe but expensive, impacts billing pipeline).
2) Apply a manual credit memo for the diff and leave metering data unchanged (fast, auditable).
3) Patch postback-service to normalize new incoming payloads and backfill past windows for the last 24-48h.
resolution:
Partial workaround applied: Billing team issued a manual credit memo of $1,820 to BrightPath Analytics to offset the provisional negative line. Autopay hold cleared per customer request.

Engineering actions planned:
- Hotfix deployed to postback-service (v1.14.3) on 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC to always interpret incoming numeric epoch_ms as UTC (unless a timezone header is provided and canonicalized). Rollout went to prod-dedicated with canary. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/412
- Backfill job scheduled to re-run hourly-accumulator for the affected windows (2026-03-10 to 2026-03-13) to ensure historical aggregates align with credit memos. Backfill ETA: 2026-03-16 12:00 UTC.
- Billing reconciliation: once backfill completes, reconcile manual credit memo against any over/under-applied tokens and adjust final invoice if needed.

Follow-ups and notes:
- Customer requested a postmortem and list of needed client-side changes (we recommend: emit RFC3339 timestamps OR include X-Event-Timezone header for ambiguous epoch_ms).
- Task created to add unit tests for timezone normalization in postback-service and to add a monitoring alert for hourly-aggregate spikes >5% compared to running median.

Status: Manual credit applied; hotfix deployed; backfill scheduled. Engineering to update once backfill and reconciliation complete.
postmortem_actions: Apply timezone normalization unit tests in metering repository (PR#412 merged).
Add alert: hourly-agg spike >5% vs rolling 7-day median to PagerDuty component.
Document recommended postback contract (RFC3339 or timezone header) in developer docs and notify dedicated customers via email/console message.
Complete hourly-accumulator backfill and run billing reconciler; cross-check with manual memo and close adjustment loop.
